list.name: Restarts
list.textFormat: process_start_time_seconds changed (crash, OOM kill or kill-service)

list.name: Flag flips
list.textFormat: runtime flag switched from the control plane

description: One screen for sale day: golden signals at the edge, business throughput, data-integrity checks, firing alerts and what customers experience. Start here, then drill into the other BreakCart dashboards.

panels.title: Gateway RPS
panels.description: Requests per second reaching the public API (gateway, /api/* routes) — the R in RED. A sudden DROP during a sale is as alarming as a spike: clients are stuck or rejected before they reach us.

panels.title: 5xx error rate
panels.description: Share of /api requests answered with 5xx over 30s — the E in RED. 4xx answers such as 409 OUT_OF_STOCK or 429 RATE_LIMITED are correct answers and are not counted; see 'Non-2xx responses by status' below.

panels.title: Latency p95
panels.description: 95th percentile gateway latency over 30s (the D in RED), estimated from the http_server_request_duration_seconds histogram. Estimates snap towards bucket bounds (0.5s, 1s, 2.5s...).

panels.title: Latency p99
panels.description: The latency SLO is 99% of /api requests under 1s, so p99 above 1s means the SLO is being violated right now. Use the heatmap to tell 'everyone is slower' from 'a slow cluster' (timeouts, lock waits). Panel link: slow traces in Jaeger.

panels.title: Gateway in-flight
panels.description: Requests the gateway is working on right now. Little's law: in-flight = throughput x latency, so at constant traffic rising latency shows up here. Load shedding rejects low-priority routes from 50% of gatewayMaxInflight (600) and checkout only at 100%. Lab: overload-collapse.

panels.title: Checkout budget burn (5m)
panels.description: How fast checkout burns its error budget (SLO: 99.5% of checkout + pay requests are not 5xx). 1x = exactly on budget. Above 14.4x on both the 5m and 1m windows the fast-burn alert pages; 6x on 30m + 5m opens a ticket. Recording rule: slo:burn_rate:rate5m.

panels.title: Orders created / min
panels.description: Checkouts that created an order, per minute (orders_checkouts_total{result="created"}). A widening gap to Paid / min means payments are failing or customers abandon at the pay step.

panels.title: Paid / min
panels.description: Orders that reached PAID per minute (orders_payments_total{result="paid"}).

panels.title: GMV / min
panels.description: Gross merchandise value of paid orders per minute, in rupees (orders_gmv_cents_total / 100).

panels.title: Payment success
panels.description: paid / all payment attempts over 1m (idempotent replays excluded). Declines (~3% by default) are normal; timeout, pending, error and rate_limited are not. Lab: payment-limbo.

panels.title: Waiting room
panels.description: Users holding a waiting-room ticket. With gateway.waitingRoom=on a sale spike becomes a queue here instead of a stampede on checkout; it drains at waitingRoomAdmitPerSec. Lab: thundering-herd.

panels.title: Consumer lag
panels.description: Order events not yet delivered to the fulfillment consumer. Lag that keeps climbing while processing is flat means the consumer is stuck on one message (poison pill retried forever). Lab: poison-pill.

panels.title: Integrity — every number here must stay 0
Oversold units
panels.description: Units sold beyond physical stock, from the control-plane integrity checker. Must be 0. Lab: oversell-race.

panels.title: Duplicate charges
panels.description: Customers charged more than once for the same order. Must be 0. Lab: double-charge.

panels.title: Orphan charges
panels.description: PSP charges without a paid order: money taken, no order. Must be 0. Lab: payment-limbo.

panels.title: Other integrity checks
panels.description: The remaining invariants. negative_stock_skus -> oversell-race, duplicate_orders -> double-charge, coupon_over_redemptions -> coupon-overrun, price_mismatches -> stale-price, stuck_orders -> payment-limbo, lost_events -> lost-events, phantom_held_units -> phantom-sellout.

panels.title: Firing alerts
panels.description: Alerts firing in Prometheus right now, read from the synthetic ALERTS series (critical first). The lab column names the lab that teaches the failure; each rule's runbook annotation points to docs/labs/<lab>.md (Prometheus UI -> Alerts, or Grafana -> Alerting -> Alert rules). An empty table means no alerts are firing.

targets.expr:
max by (alertname, severity, lab, service, target) (ALERTS{alertstate="firing", severity="critical"}) * 3
or max by (alertname, severity, lab, service, target) (ALERTS{alertstate="firing", severity="warning"}) * 2
or max by (alertname, severity, lab, service, target) (ALERTS{alertstate="firing", severity!~"critical|warning"})

panels.title: Service health
panels.description: up == 1 when Prometheus scraped /metrics within the 2s timeout. A service whose event loop is blocked longer than that also shows DOWN — exactly what a load balancer health check would see.

panels.title: Gateway latency heatmap
panels.description: Every /api request placed in its latency bucket per time slice; brighter = more requests. Healthy is one tight band. A second band at 5s/10s/30s is requests waiting for timeouts; a band drifting upwards is queueing.

panels.title: Gateway latency percentiles
panels.description: p50 / p95 / p99 from the same histogram; the dashed red line is the 1s latency SLO. p50 flat but p99 climbing = a minority of requests is stuck (lock waits, slow dependency, GC). All three rising together = the whole service is saturated.

panels.title: Requests by route
panels.description: Request rate per API route (stacked). At the sale spike compare /api/checkout with /api/queue/status: polling the waiting room is cheap, a stampede on checkout is not.

panels.title: Non-2xx responses by status
panels.description: Responses that are not 2xx. 409 = business rejections (OUT_OF_STOCK, QUEUE_REQUIRED, PRICE_CHANGED...), 429 = rate limited, 403 = bot suspected, 402 = payment declined, 503 = shed (OVERLOADED) or upstream unavailable, 504 = timeout. 5xx in red.

panels.title: Error responses by code
panels.description: Gateway error responses by the error code in the body (http_server_errors_total). It separates what one status hides: 409 is OUT_OF_STOCK, QUEUE_REQUIRED, PRICE_CHANGED, COUPON_EXHAUSTED or SALE_NOT_STARTED; 503 is OVERLOADED (shed) or UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE. Server-side failures (INTERNAL, INJECTED_FAULT, UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE, PAYMENT_TIMEOUT) in red.

panels.title: Customer-experienced p95 by step
panels.description: Latency per funnel step as the virtual customers measured it (client side). It includes what the server never sees: connection setup, queueing in front of the gateway, client retries. Much worse than the server p95? See the Load Generator dashboard.

panels.title: Sessions by result
panels.description: Finished virtual-user sessions per minute. converted = paid order; sold_out = wanted stock that ran out (check phantom-sellout if units are actually held); blocked = bot protection; failed = an error the customer could not get past.

panels.title: Checkout & payment outcomes
panels.description: Business outcomes per minute. Checkout: created, out_of_stock, price_changed, coupon_exhausted, error, duplicate_replayed, in_progress. Payment: paid, declined, timeout, pending, error, rate_limited, replayed, expired.

panels.title: Circuit breakers
panels.description: Every circuit breaker, caller -> target. OPEN (red): calls fail fast without touching the dependency. HALF-OPEN (yellow): a few probes test recovery. Labs: retry-storm, cascading-failure.

panels.title: Event loop lag p99
panels.description: p99 event-loop delay per service. Node runs your JavaScript on one thread, so anything synchronous (pretty-printed logs, huge JSON, CPU burn, GC) delays every request in that process. Dashed line: 200ms alert threshold. Labs: logging-meltdown, gc-pauses.

panels.title: DB pool waiting
panels.description: Requests queued for a pooled Postgres connection, per service. If waiting > 0 while idle == 0 the pool is exhausted — see lab pool-exhaustion and the Data Layer dashboard.

panels.title: Active chaos
panels.description: Fault injection currently switched on, per service (chaos_active == 1). Check this first: a symptom that matches an injected fault is not a code bug. Enable the 'Chaos' annotation toggle to see when it started.
